metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets France

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for France using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting typically relies on PISA sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used for variance estimation, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported uncertainty (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicates that standard PISA variance estimation procedures were applied, but the specific technical details are deferred to the PISA Reader’s Guide and annexes referenced in the document.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because this document is a descriptive results factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related associations, rather than reporting an empirical student-level predictive model that requires explicit PV combining rules. The factsheet also does not describe any missing-data strategy (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) for the analytic dataset used to compute the reported estimates. Therefore, missing-data handling is treated as not reported because the necessary methodological details are not provided in the excerpt.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports France-specific results for the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test. It states that 6,770 students in 282 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 781,300 15-year-olds (an estimated 93% of the total population of 15-year-olds). No additional analytic inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., specific task completion thresholds, missing-data exclusions, or subpopulation restrictions) are described in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking outcomes for 15-year-old students in France. PISA 2022 Creative Thinking was administered in 64 countries/economies (including France) and consists of 32 open-ended tasks scored by human judgement using detailed rubrics. The test measures three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating/improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. For France, the mean creative thinking score is 32 on a 60-point scale, which is on par with the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency distributions (78% at Level 3+; 26% at Level 5/6) and descriptive associations with mathematics and reading performance, including that 25% of the variation in creative thinking is uniquely explained by mathematics performance in France. It further highlights within-France gaps by socioeconomic status and gender, and reports how students’ beliefs/attitudes and school pedagogies relate to creative thinking performance, while noting COVID-19-related data collection challenges and the need for caution for some countries/economies.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (descriptive reporting) rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not train or evaluate machine learning models, does not specify PV combining rules or missing-data procedures, and does not provide an analytic pipeline with model metrics that would populate ML-specific fields. The absence of main_findings rows and confounder lists reflects the document’s purpose: communicating benchmarked performance levels, distributions, and descriptive relationships from the PISA 2022 database rather than estimating predictive models in the text provided.
